newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico aims for net natural gas exports - ass'n.
newsitem.headline: Mexico aims for net natural gas exports - ass'n.

text.p: Mexico should reduce natural gas imports in 1997 and boost exports through increased production by state oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex), the Mexican Natural Gas Association said Thursday.

"Mexico should convert itself, but not immediately, to a net exporting country. We should try to lower imports in accordance with greater (natural gas) resources," association general manager Jorge Rebolledo Costes told reporters.
Pemex imports natural gas from the United States, mostly in Mexico's northern region, and principally exports south of its borders to Central America.

Natural gas exploration projects are planned in 1997 at Burgos Basin, in the northern state of Tamaulipas, and the nation's largest oil producing field, Cantarell, an offshore site in the Gulf of Mexico. Pemex's natural gas unit plans to spend 1.69 billion pesos during the year.

"Pemex has sufficient production capacity, and will have even more from Burgos and Cantarell explorations, so that it whould not need to import," new association president Angelica Fuentes said. The association is composed of national and foreign natural gas distributors.
She said Mexico's natural gas imports along the U.S. border are currently convenient because of low transport costs, compared with transport costs from Pemex installations.

Mexico imported 84 million cubic feet per day (cfd) of natural gas in 1996, compared with 173 million cfd in 1995, according to Pemex figures. The state monopoly exported 37 million cfd in last year, compared with 22 million cfd in 1995.
